hook.en: ISC grammar often asks you to rewrite a sentence beginning with given words, without changing its meaning. It tests whether you really control English structures.

objectives.en: Rewrite sentences with no sooner, hardly, too…to, so…that, unless and despite
Change between active and passive, direct and indirect speech
Keep the meaning and the tense exact

narration.en: ISC grammar often asks you to rewrite a sentence beginning with given words, without changing its meaning. It tests whether you really control English structures.

body.en: As soon as he arrived, it rained → No sooner had he arrived than it rained → Hardly had he arrived when it rained (inversion after the negative adverb). He is too weak to walk → He is so weak that he cannot walk. If you do not work, you will fail → Unless you work, you will fail. Although it was raining, they played → Despite the rain, they played / In spite of the rain … Not only did she sing, but she also danced. Scarcely had … when; Neither … nor; Were I you, I would … (inverted conditional).

points.en: Although ↔ Despite / In spite of + noun

text.en: As soon as the bell rang, the students rushed out.
No sooner had the bell rung than the students rushed out.

say.en: Despite takes a noun or -ing form, not a clause.

text.en: Although he was ill, he attended the meeting.
Despite being ill, he attended the meeting.
The committee has approved the plan.
The plan has been approved by the committee.

say.en: Reported speech shifts the tense back.

text.en: She said that she was leaving the next day.

narration.en: Let us build up transformations worked on the board, one step at a time.

prompt.en: Match each sentence with its correct transformation.

narration.en: Match each sentence with its correct transformation.

left.en: As soon as she saw me, she smiled.

right.en: No sooner did she see me than she smiled.

left.en: The box is too heavy for me to lift.

right.en: The box is so heavy that I cannot lift it.

left.en: If you do not hurry, you will miss the bus.

right.en: Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.

left.en: Although it was late, we continued.

right.en: In spite of the late hour, we continued.

left.en: He not only wrote the song but also sang it.

right.en: Not only did he write the song, but he also sang it.

explanation.en: Each pair keeps the meaning and the tense; negative openings take inversion (did she, did he).

body.en: Active to passive: the object becomes the subject, the verb becomes be (in the same tense) + past participle, and the doer may follow with by. Direct to indirect speech: remove the quotation marks, use a reporting verb (said, told, asked, requested), change pronouns, shift tenses back one step after a past reporting verb (is → was, will → would, has → had), and change words of time and place (today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, here → there). Questions become statements with if/whether or the question word.

points.en: today → that day; tomorrow → the next day

passage.en: Hardly had we sat down __1__ the lights went out. She is so tired that she __2__ walk any further. Were I in your place, I __3__ apologise. He asked me __4__ I had finished the work.

explanation.en: Hardly … when; so … that … cannot; inverted conditional Were I … I would; a reported yes/no question uses whether (or if).

problem.en: Rewrite: "Although the road was blocked, the ambulance reached the hospital in time." Begin: (a) Despite … (b) The road …

steps.en: (a) Despite takes a noun phrase: Despite the blocked road, the ambulance reached the hospital in time.
(b) Keep the contrast with but or yet: The road was blocked, but the ambulance reached the hospital in time.
Check that the tense (past) and the meaning (contrast) are unchanged.

answer.en: (a) Despite the blocked road, … (b) The road was blocked, but …
